verses.1:1: The words of Amos, which came to be in Akkarim in Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.1:2: And he said, "The Lord sounded forth from Zion, and from Jerusalem He gave His voice; and the pastures of the shepherds mourned, and the summit of Carmel dried up."
verses.1:3: And the Lord said, "For the three impieties of Damascus, and for the four, I will not turn away from it, because they sawed with iron saws the pregnant women of those in Gilead;
verses.1:4: and I will send out fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the foundations of the son of Hader;
verses.1:5: and I will shatter the bars of Damascus, and I will utterly destroy the inhabitants from the plain of On, and I will cut down a tribe from the men of Haran, and the chosen people of Syria will be taken captive," says the Lord.
verses.1:6: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of Gaza, and for the four, I will not turn away from them, because they took captive the captives of Solomon, to shut them up into Idumea;
verses.1:7: and I will send out fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it will devour its foundations.
verses.1:8: And I will utterly destroy the inhabitants from Ashdod, and a tribe will be removed from Ashkelon, and I will bring My hand upon Ekron, and the rest of the foreigners will perish," says the Lord.
verses.1:9: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of Tyre, and for the four, I will not turn away from it, because they shut up the captives of Solomon into Idumea, and did not remember a covenant of brothers;
verses.1:10: and I will send out fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it will devour its foundations."
verses.1:11: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of Idumea, and for the four, I will not turn away from them, because they pursued his brother with a sword, and he ravaged a mother upon the earth, and he seized his horror for a testimony, and he kept his onslaught for victory;
verses.1:12: and I will send out fire into Teman, and it will devour the foundations of its walls."
verses.1:13: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of the sons of Ammon, and for the four, I will not turn away from him, because they ripped open the pregnant women of the Gileadites, so that they might enlarge their own borders;
verses.1:14: and I will kindle fire upon the walls of Rabbah, and it will devour its foundations with a shout in the day of war, and it will be shaken in the days of its end;
verses.1:15: and its kings will go in captivity, their priests and their rulers together," says the Lord.
verses.2:1: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of Moab, and for the four, I will not turn away from it, because they burned up the bones of the king of Idumea into lime;
verses.2:2: and I will send out fire upon Moab, and it will devour the foundations of its cities, and Moab will die in weakness, with a shout and with the sound of a trumpet;
verses.2:3: and I will utterly destroy a judge from it, and I will kill all who belong to it with him," says the Lord.
verses.2:4: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of the sons of Judah, and for the four, I will not turn away from him, because they rejected the law of the Lord, and did not keep His ordinances, and their vain things which they made led them astray, after which their fathers followed;
verses.2:5: and I will send out fire upon Judah, and it will devour the foundations of Jerusalem."
verses.2:6: This is what the Lord says: "For the three impieties of Israel, and for the four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous man for silver, and a needy man for sandals,
verses.2:7: which tread upon the dust of the earth; and they struck the heads of the poor with their fists, and turned aside the way of the humble, and a son and his father went in to the same servant girl, so that they might profane the name of their God;
verses.2:8: and binding their garments with cords, they made curtains next to the altar, and they drank wine from extortion in the house of their God.
verses.2:9: Yet I removed the Amorite from before them, whose height was like the height of a cedar, and he was strong as an oak; and I dried up his fruit from above and his roots from below;
verses.2:10: and I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and I led you around in the wilderness forty years to inherit the land of the Amorites;
verses.2:11: and I took from your sons for prophets, and from your young men for consecration. Are these things not so, sons of Israel?" says the Lord.
verses.2:12: "And you gave the consecrated ones wine to drink, and you commanded the prophets, saying, 'You must by no means prophesy.'
verses.2:13: Therefore, look, I roll beneath you in the way the wagon full of straw rolls;
verses.2:14: and flight will perish from a runner, and the mighty man will by no means keep hold of his strength, and the warrior will by no means save his life,
verses.2:15: and the archer will by no means stand firm, and the one swift with his feet will by no means escape safely, nor will the horseman by any means save his life,
verses.2:16: and the mighty man will by no means find his heart in acts of power; the naked man will pursue on that day," says the Lord.
verses.3:1: Hear this word that the Lord spoke against you, house of Israel, and against every tribe that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.3:2: "Only you have I known out of all the tribes of the earth; therefore I will execute vengeance upon you for all your sins."
verses.3:3: Will two walk together at all unless they become acquainted with one another?
verses.3:4: Will a lion roar from its forest when it has no prey? Will a young lion give its voice from its den at all unless it has seized something?
verses.3:5: Will a bird fall to the ground without a bird-catcher? Will a trap be sprung upon the ground without catching anything?
verses.3:6: Will a trumpet sound in a city and people not be terrified? Will there be evil in a city that the Lord has not done?
verses.3:7: For the Lord God will by no means do a thing unless He reveals instruction to His servants the prophets.
verses.3:8: A lion will roar, and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?
verses.3:9: "Proclaim to the regions among the Assyrians and over the regions of Egypt, and say, 'Gather together upon the mountain of Samaria, and see many astonishing things in her midst and the oppression that is in her.'
verses.3:10: And she did not know what will be before her," says the Lord, "those who store up injustice and misery in their regions."
verses.3:11: Therefore, this is what the Lord God says: "Tyre, your land will be laid waste all around, and he will bring down your strength from you, and your regions will be plundered."
verses.3:12: This is what the Lord says: "Just as when the shepherd snatches from the mouth of the lion two legs or a lobe of an ear, so the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be snatched out opposite the tribe, and priests in Damascus."
verses.3:13: "Hear and testify against the house of Jacob," says the Lord God, the Almighty,
verses.3:14: "for on the day when I execute vengeance for the impieties of Israel upon him, I will also execute vengeance upon the altars of Bethel, and the horns of the altar will be torn down and will fall to the ground;
verses.3:15: I will demolish and strike the colonnaded house upon the summer house, and ivory houses will perish, and many other houses will be added," says the Lord.
verses.4:1: Hear this word, heifers of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who say to their masters, "Give to us so that we may drink."
verses.4:2: The Lord swears by His holy things: "Look, days are coming upon you, and they will take you with weapons, and fiery pests will throw those with you into cauldrons heated from below,
verses.4:3: and you will be carried out naked opposite one another, and you will be cast away to Mount Romman," says the Lord.
verses.4:4: You entered Bethel and acted ungodly, and at Gilgal you multiplied acting ungodly; and you brought your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes for the three-day period;
verses.4:5: and they read a law outside and called for confessions. Proclaim that the sons of Israel loved these things, says the Lord God.
verses.4:6: And I will give you aching of teeth in all your cities, and a lack of bread in all your places, and you did not turn back to Me, says the Lord.
verses.4:7: And I withheld the rain from you three months before the vintage; and I will send rain upon one city, but upon another city I will not send rain; one portion will be rained upon, and a portion upon which I will not send rain will dry up.
verses.4:8: And two and three cities will gather together into one city to drink water, and they will certainly not be satisfied, and you did not turn back to Me, says the Lord.
verses.4:9: I struck you with scorching heat and with blight; you multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards and your fig groves and your olive groves, and not even so did you turn back to Me, says the Lord.
verses.4:10: I sent out death among you in the way of Egypt, and I killed your young men with the sword along with the captivity of your horses, and I brought up your camps in fire in your anger, and not even so did you turn back to Me, says the Lord.
verses.4:11: I overthrew you just as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched out of fire, and not even so did you turn back to Me, says the Lord.
verses.4:12: Therefore I will do thus to you, Israel; yet because I will do thus to you, prepare yourself to call upon your God, Israel.
verses.4:13: For He who establishes thunder and creates wind and declares His anointed to people, who makes dawn and mist, treading upon the heights of the earth: the Lord God Almighty is His name.
verses.5:1: Hear this word of the Lord which I take up over you as a lamentation: "The house of Israel
verses.5:2: has fallen; it will never rise again; the virgin of Israel has stumbled upon his land; there is no one who will raise her up."
verses.5:3: Therefore, this is what the Lord, the Lord says: "The city from which a thousand went out will have a hundred left, and the one from which a hundred went out will have ten left for the house of Israel."
verses.5:4: For this is what the Lord says to the house of Israel: "Seek Me, and you will live;
verses.5:5: and do not seek Bethel, and do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath, because Gilgal will surely be taken captive, and Bethel will be as though it does not exist."
verses.5:6: Seek the Lord and live, so that the house of Joseph may not blaze up like fire and devour it, and there will be no one to quench it for the house of Israel.
verses.5:7: He who does justice on high, and placed righteousness on the earth;
verses.5:8: He who makes all things and transforms them, and turns shadow into the morning, and darkens day into night; He who summons the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth, the Lord is His name;
verses.5:9: He who apportions ruin upon strength, and brings misery upon a fortress.
verses.5:10: They hated one who reproves in the gates, and they abhorred a devout word.
verses.5:11: Therefore, because they were beating the poor with fists, and you accepted choice gifts from them, you built houses of hewn stone, yet you will certainly not dwell in them; you planted desirable vineyards, yet you will certainly not drink the wine from them.
verses.5:12: For I know your many acts of ungodliness, and your sins are strong, trampling a righteous person, taking bribes and turning aside the needy in the gates.
verses.5:13: Therefore the one who understands will keep silent in that time, because it is a time of evils.
verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and thus the Lord God Almighty will be with you; just as you said,
verses.5:15: "We have hated evil things and loved good things," so restore justice in the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
verses.5:16: Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: "In all the squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets it will be said, 'Woe, woe!' A farmer will be called to mourning and wailing, and to those who know lamentation,
verses.5:17: and in all streets there will be wailing, because I will pass through your midst," said the Lord.
verses.5:18: Woe to you who desire the day of the Lord! Why is this day of the Lord for you? And it is darkness and not light,
verses.5:19: just as when a man flees from before a lion and a bear falls upon him, and he leaps into his house and leans his hands against the wall, and a snake bites him.
verses.5:20: Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light? And is it not gloom having no brightness?
verses.5:21: I have hated, I have rejected your festivals, and I will by no means smell sacrifices in your festive assemblies.
verses.5:22: For if you bring Me burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look upon your displays of deliverance.
verses.5:23: Remove from Me the sound of your songs, and I will not listen to the music of your instruments;
verses.5:24: and justice will roll like water, and righteousness like an impassable torrent.
verses.5:25: Did you offer Me slaughtered animals and sacrifices in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
verses.5:26: And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, their images which you made for yourselves;
verses.5:27: and I will deport you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; God Almighty is His name.
verses.6:1: Woe to those who despise Zion and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria! They harvested the foremost of the nations, and they themselves entered. House of Israel,
verses.6:2: cross over, all of you, and see, and pass through from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down from there to Gath of the foreigners, the mightiest of all these kingdoms, whether their borders are greater than your borders.
verses.6:3: Those who come to an evil day, who draw near and take hold of false sabbaths,
verses.6:4: who sleep on ivory beds and live in luxury on their couches, and eat young goats from flocks and suckling calves from the midst of herds,
verses.6:5: who clap to the sound of the instruments; they reckoned them as enduring and not as fleeting;
verses.6:6: who drink strained wine and anoint themselves with the finest perfumes, and suffered nothing over the ruin of Joseph.
verses.6:7: Therefore now they will be captives at the head of the rulers, and the neighing of horses will be removed from Ephraim.
verses.6:8: For the Lord swore by Himself: "I abhor all the arrogance of Jacob, and I have hated his lands, and I will remove a city with all who inhabit it."
verses.6:9: And it will be that if ten are left in one house, they will die, and the remaining ones will be left,
verses.6:10: and their relatives will take them and strive hard to carry their bones out of the house; and he will say to those in charge of the house, "Is there still anyone with you?" And he will say, "No longer." And he will say, "Be silent, so as not to name the name of the Lord."
verses.6:11: For look, the Lord commands, and He will strike the great house with fractures and the small house with cracks.
verses.6:12: Will horses race on rocks? Will they keep silent among mares? Yet you turned justice into fury, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness,
verses.6:13: you who rejoice over nothing, who say, "Did we not gain horns by our strength?"
verses.6:14: For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel, says the Lord of hosts, and they will oppress you so that you cannot enter Hamath, and as far as the torrent of the west.
verses.7:1: Thus the Lord God showed me, and look, a brood of locusts coming at dawn, and look, one wingless locust, Gog the King.
verses.7:2: And it will be, if it finishes devouring the grass of the land—and I said, "Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who will raise up Jacob? For he is very small;
verses.7:3: relent, Lord, concerning this." "This also will not be," says the Lord.
verses.7:4: Thus the Lord showed me, and look, the Lord summoned judgment by fire, and it devoured the great abyss, and it devoured the portion of the Lord.
verses.7:5: And I said, "Lord, please cease! Who will raise up Jacob? For he is very small;
verses.7:6: relent, Lord, concerning this." "This also will certainly not happen," says the Lord.
verses.7:7: Thus the Lord showed me, and look, He was standing on a wall of adamant, and in His hand was adamant.
verses.7:8: And the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "Adamant." And the Lord said to me, "Look, I am setting adamant in the midst of My people Israel; I will never again pass them by;
verses.7:9: and the altars of laughter will be destroyed, and the rites of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
verses.7:10: And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land will not be able to bear all his words.
verses.7:11: For this is what Amos says: 'By the sword Jeroboam will die, and Israel will be led captive from its land.'"
verses.7:12: And Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go, depart into the land of Judah, and live out your life there, and there you will prophesy;
verses.7:13: but at Bethel you will no longer prophesy, for it is a king's sanctuary, and it is a house of the kingdom."
verses.7:14: And Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was not a prophet, nor a son of a prophet; rather, I was a goatherd and one who nips sycamore figs.
verses.7:15: And the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
verses.7:16: And now, hear the word of the Lord: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and you must never stir up a crowd against the house of Jacob.'
verses.7:17: Therefore this is what the Lord says: 'Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your land will be measured out with a cord, and you yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will be led captive from its land.'" Thus the Lord, the Lord showed me,
verses.8:2: and look, a bird-catcher's basket. And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A bird-catcher's basket." And the Lord said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will no longer pass them by.
verses.8:3: And the paneled ceilings of the temple will wail in that day," says the Lord, the Lord. "Many are the fallen in every place; I will cast silence."
verses.8:4: Hear these things now, you who crush the needy in the morning and oppress the poor from the land,
verses.8:5: saying, "When will the month pass by so that we may sell, and the Sabbaths so that we may open a storehouse to make a small measure, and to enlarge the weight and make an unjust scale,
verses.8:6: to acquire even the poor with silver, and a lowly person in exchange for sandals, and from all produce we will trade?"
verses.8:7: The Lord swears by the arrogance of Jacob: "Surely all your deeds will not be forgotten forever,
verses.8:8: and because of these things, will the earth not be troubled, and will everyone who dwells in it not mourn? And destruction will rise like a river, and it will go down like the river of Egypt."
verses.8:9: "And it will happen in that day," says the Lord, the Lord, "that the sun will set at noon, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in the daytime;
verses.8:10: and I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring sackcloth upon every waist, and baldness upon every head; and I will make him like the mourning for a beloved one, and those with him like a day of pain."
verses.8:11: "Look, days are coming," says the Lord, "when I will send out a famine upon the land—not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine for hearing the word of the Lord.
verses.8:12: And the waters of the sea will be shaken, and from the north to the east they will run about, seeking the word of the Lord, and they will certainly not find it.
verses.8:13: In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint from thirst,
verses.8:14: those who swear by the propitiation of Samaria, and those who say, 'Your God lives, Dan, and your God lives, Beersheba!' And they will fall and never rise again."
verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing on the altar, and He said, "Strike upon the mercy seat, and the gateways will be shaken, and cut through onto the heads of all; and the remnant of them I will kill with the sword. No one who flees from among them will escape, and no survivor from among them will be saved.
verses.9:2: If they hide themselves in Hades, from there My hand will pull them up; and if they go up into heaven, from there I will bring them down;
verses.9:3: if they hide themselves on the peak of Carmel, from there I will search out and take them; and if they sink down from My eyes into the depths of the sea, there I will command the dragon, and it will bite them;
verses.9:4: and if they go in captivity before the face of their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them; and I will fix My eyes upon them for evil and not for good."
verses.9:5: And the Lord, the Lord God Almighty, the One who touches the earth and shakes it, and all who dwell in it will mourn; and its destruction will rise like a river, and it will go down like the river of Egypt;
verses.9:6: the One who builds His ascent into heaven, and founds His promise upon the earth, the One who calls for the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth; the Lord Almighty is His name.
verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to Me, sons of Israel?" says the Lord. "Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the foreigners from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from a pit?"
verses.9:8: "Look, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of the sinners, and I will remove it from the face of the earth; yet I will not completely remove the house of Jacob," says the Lord.
verses.9:9: "For I am commanding, and I will winnow the house of Israel among all the nations, just as winnowing is done in a winnowing basket, and not a fragment will fall to the ground.
verses.9:10: By the sword all the sinners of My people will die, those who say, 'Evils will certainly not draw near nor come upon us.'"
verses.9:11: "In that day I will raise up the tent of David that has fallen, and I will rebuild its fallen parts, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will rebuild it just as in the ancient days,
verses.9:12: so that the remnant of mankind may seek, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called," says the Lord who does these things.
verses.9:13: "Look, days are coming," says the Lord, "when the harvest will overtake the vintage, and the grape will ripen at sowing time, and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will be thickly wooded;
verses.9:14: and I will bring back the captivity of My people Israel, and they will build the destroyed cities and dwell in them, and they will plant a vineyard and drink their wine, and they will plant gardens and eat their fruits;
verses.9:15: and I will plant them upon their land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land that I have given them," says the Lord God Almighty.

notes.1:1: The Greek text reads "which came to be in Akkarim" (transliterating the Hebrew word for "shepherds" as a place name) and "concerning Jerusalem," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "who was among the shepherds" and "concerning Israel."
notes.1:3: Throughout chapters 1-2, the Greek formula "I will not turn away from it/him/them" renders the Hebrew expression for not revoking punishment, and here specifies sawing "the pregnant women of those in Gilead" with iron saws (compare Hebrew "threshed Gilead with iron sledges").
notes.1:5: The Greek preserves distinct proper names and readings here and in verse 4: "son of Hader" (Hebrew "Ben-hadad"), "plain of On" (Hebrew "Valley of Aven"), "a tribe from the men of Haran" (Hebrew "the scepter-bearer from Beth-eden"), and "the chosen people of Syria" (Hebrew "to Kir").
notes.1:6: Here and in verse 9, the Greek reads "captives of Solomon" (reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew for "a whole captivity") and uses the Greek territorial name "Idumea" for Edom; in verse 8, "foreigners" is the Septuagint's standard rendering for the Philistines.
notes.1:11: The Greek diverges sharply from the Hebrew, reading "ravaged a mother upon the earth," "seized his horror for a testimony," and "kept his onslaught for victory," followed in verse 12 by "the foundations of its walls" (where the Hebrew has "the citadels of Bozrah").
notes.2:3: The Greek text reads simply "all who belong to it" (literally "all of hers"), omitting the noun "officials/princes" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.2:7: In Greek, "which tread upon the dust of the earth" is neuter plural modifying "sandals" at the end of verse 6, followed by "struck the heads of the poor with their fists" and "the name of their God" (Hebrew "My holy name").
notes.2:13: The Greek translates the verb as "roll" ("I roll beneath you in the way the wagon full of straw rolls"), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes pressing down or groaning beneath a cart loaded with sheaves.
notes.2:16: The Greek reads "will by no means find his heart in acts of power; the naked man will pursue on that day," using the active future of "pursue" (unlike the Hebrew "the stout of heart among the mighty will flee away naked").
notes.3:3: The Greek reads "unless they become acquainted with one another" (based on the Hebrew root for "know") rather than "unless they have agreed to meet," and in verse 7 reads "reveals instruction" where the Hebrew has "reveals His secret counsel."
notes.3:9: The Greek reads "among the Assyrians" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "in Ashdod"), "many astonishing things," and in verse 10 "she did not know what will be before her" (Hebrew "they do not know how to do right").
notes.3:11: The Greek reads the proper name "Tyre" (interpreting the Hebrew word for "adversary" as the city name), leaving the subject of "he will bring down" unexpressed.
notes.3:12: The Greek reads "opposite the tribe, and priests in Damascus," interpreting the Hebrew terms for a couch and damask bed as "tribe," "Damascus," and "priests."
notes.3:15: The Greek reads "demolish and strike the colonnaded house" (Hebrew "winter house") and "many other houses will be added" (reading the Hebrew verb as "be added" rather than "come to an end").
notes.4:2: Greek τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ is plural and may mean neuter "His holy things" (sanctuary) or masculine "His holy ones," where the Hebrew has "His holiness." The Greek also reads "with weapons" and "fiery pests will throw those with you into cauldrons heated from below," differing markedly from the Hebrew wording.
notes.4:3: Greek Ῥομμάν ("Romman") is a Septuagint-distinct place name where the Masoretic Text has Harmon.
notes.4:5: The Septuagint reads "they read a law outside and called for confessions," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text's leavened thank offering and freewill offerings.
notes.4:10: Greek "in fire ... in your anger" differs from the Masoretic Text ("the stench ... into your nostrils") through reading the Hebrew consonants as "fire" and translating the word for "nose/anger" in its sense "anger."
notes.4:13: The Septuagint reads βροντήν ("thunder") where the Hebrew has "mountains," and τὸν χριστὸν αὐτοῦ ("His anointed," also readable as "His Christ") where the Masoretic Text has "what is his thought." Greek πνεῦμα can mean either "wind" or "spirit."
notes.5:3: Greek κύριος Κύριος ("the Lord, the Lord") literally reflects the double Hebrew divine title Adonai YHWH.
notes.5:5: Greek τὸ φρέαρ τοῦ ὅρκου ("the Well of the Oath") is the Septuagint's literal translation of the place name Beersheba.
notes.5:7: The Septuagint renders this verse in the singular as part of the hymn to God (continuing into 5:8-9) and reads "on high" (εἰς ὕψος) where the Masoretic Text addresses human oppressors turning justice "to wormwood." In 5:8 the Greek likewise has "all things and transforms them" where the Hebrew names Pleiades and Orion.
notes.5:15: The Septuagint links "just as you said" at the end of 5:14 to first-person plural perfects here ("We have hated ... and loved"), quoting Israel's claim rather than issuing imperatives as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.5:26: The Septuagint reads "the tent of Moloch" and "the star of your god Rephan" (Greek Ῥαιφάν), a well-known Septuagint reading quoted in Acts 7:43 where the Masoretic Text has Sikkuth and Kiyyun.
notes.6:2: Greek πάντες ("all of you") stands where the Masoretic Text has the city Calneh, and Ἑμὰθ Ῥαββά transliterates "Hamath Rabbah" (Hebrew "Hamath the great"). Greek ἀλλοφύλων ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines.
notes.6:3: Greek "who come to an evil day" and "false sabbaths" (σαββάτων ψευδῶν) differ from the Masoretic Text ("who put far away the day of disaster" and "the seat of violence").
notes.6:7: Greek "the neighing of horses will be removed from Ephraim" differs sharply from the Masoretic Text ("the revelry of those who stretch out shall pass away").
notes.6:12: Greek εἰ παρασιωπήσονται ἐν θηλείαις ("Will they keep silent among mares/females?") reflects reading the Hebrew root as "be silent" rather than "plow" (Masoretic Text: "or does one plow there with oxen?").
notes.6:14: Greek "so that you cannot enter Hamath" and "the torrent of the west" (δυσμῶν) translate the Hebrew place expressions Lebo-hamath and the Brook of the Arabah as descriptive phrases, with ὡς functioning for ἕως ("as far as").
notes.7:1: The Greek reads 'Gog the King' for the leading wingless locust, diverging sharply from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'the king's mowings' and introducing an eschatological figure.
notes.7:3: Here (and again in 7:6) the Greek has an imperative plea from Amos, 'relent, Lord, concerning this,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a narrative statement that the Lord relented.
notes.7:7: Greek 'adamas' ('adamant', the hardest metal or stone) corresponds to the rare Hebrew term usually rendered 'plumb line' or 'tin.'
notes.7:9: The Greek translates the Hebrew name Isaac literally as 'laughter' ('altars of laughter') and renders 'sanctuaries' as 'rites' ('teletai').
notes.7:17: The title 'the Lord, the Lord' renders the doubled Greek 'kyrios Kyrios.' The final clause ('Thus the Lord, the Lord showed me,') begins the fourth vision—usually numbered 8:1—so chapter 8 begins at 8:2 in this Greek text.
notes.8:2: Greek 'angos ixeutou' ('a bird-catcher's basket') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'basket of summer fruit,' which puns on the Hebrew word for 'end.'
notes.8:3: Greek 'phatnomata' ('paneled ceilings') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'songs,' and the final clause reads a first-person future verb ('I will cast silence').
notes.8:7: The Greek conditional particle 'ei' reflects a Hebrew oath idiom carrying strong negation ('surely ... not'), and 'eis nikos' (lit. 'to victory') is a standard Septuagint idiom meaning 'forever' or 'completely.'
notes.8:10: Greek 'agapetou' ('a beloved one') renders the Hebrew for 'an only son,' and 'those with him' ('tous met' autou') differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'its end.'
notes.8:12: The Greek reads 'the waters of the sea will be shaken,' diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'they shall wander from sea to sea.'
notes.9:1: Greek 'hilasterion' ('mercy seat', the term used for the lid of the ark) replaces the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'capital' of a pillar.
notes.9:6: Greek 'epangelian' ('promise') diverges from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'vault' or 'band.'
notes.9:7: The Greek uses 'foreigners' ('allophyloi', its standard rendering for the Philistines), 'Cappadocia' (for Hebrew Caphtor), and 'from a pit' (for Hebrew 'from Kir').
notes.9:12: The Greek reads 'so that the remnant of mankind may seek' (reflecting the text quoted in Acts 15:17, without an explicit object after 'seek' here), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'that they may possess the remnant of Edom.'
notes.9:13: The Greek reads 'the harvest will overtake the vintage, and the grape will ripen at sowing time' and 'thickly wooded' ('symphytoi'), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's imagery of the plowman, grape-treader, and melting hills.
